claims.text: CoCrFeNiMo-type HEA coatings can contain FCC and σ phases.
The cited CoCrFeNiMo-type material has a eutectic microstructure.
The microstructure specifically consists of an FCC matrix containing embedded σ-phase precipitates.
The FCC phase is ductile.
The σ phase is harder than the FCC matrix and strengthens the coating.
The σ phase is electrochemically more noble than the FCC matrix.
Multiphase structures in CoCrFeNiMo-type coatings induce galvanic effects and comparatively inferior corrosion resistance.
The galvanic cells are localized specifically at FCC/σ interphase boundaries.
FCC/σ interphase boundaries are stress concentrators and zones of differential electrochemical potential.
Elevated temperature enhances galvanic corrosion at the phase boundaries.
Protective oxide or passive films form on the alloy phases.
Mechanical sliding repeatedly ruptures the protective oxide films at micro-galvanic interfaces.
Film rupture exposes fresh metal to localized corrosive attack and cyclic oxidation.
The repeated film-formation and rupture cycle produces synergistically accelerated material removal by wear and corrosion.
Oxidative wear is a dominant wear mechanism in a CoCrFeNiMo coating.
A multiphase eutectic alloy will have a higher total degradation rate than a same-composition, single-phase baseline under simultaneous high-temperature wear and corrosion.
The multiphase alloy will have greater wear loss than the matched single-phase baseline because of accelerated oxide-film rupture.
The multiphase alloy will have a higher corrosion rate than the matched single-phase baseline because of local galvanic attack.
The proposed mechanism applies during sliding in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at approximately 600°C.
The alloy can be converted from multiphase to single phase through compositional tuning or thermal treatment while retaining the same nominal composition.

contradictions.description: Compositional tuning is offered as a way to create the single-phase comparator, while the comparator is also required to retain the same nominal composition. Compositional tuning would ordinarily change that nominal composition; only the heat-treatment route is consistent with the stated matched-composition control.
